subject: Recap + confirmation requested: NovaCare data handling & next steps
participants_external: anna.lewis@novacare.com (Anna Lewis, Head of Data Platforms)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@novacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 13:15:00 -0400
Subject: Recap: NovaCare discovery — data handling & next steps

Anna — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything on the same page.

Key commitments we discussed:
- Training on customer data: NovaCare requires an explicit opt-out — Redwood will not use NovaCare customer data to train or improve models.
- Logging & retention: inference logs retained for 30 days by default; longer retention requires approval.
- PII handling: we will not store raw PII in logs; sensitive fields will be hashed (SHA-256) and salted where feasible.
- Data residency: processing and logs for your tenant will be restricted to EU region (Frankfurt / eu-central-1).
- Compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we will provide relevant evidence as requested.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please reply to confirm the bullets above capture NovaCare requirements as-is (or list adjustments).
2) Once confirmed, we will send a short addendum to the contract that enumerates the training opt-out and residency requirements for signature (DocuSign).
3) I will loop in Marissa (billing/ops) and Ben (legal) to prepare the addendum and timeline; target sign-and-live within 2 weeks of agreement if that works for you.

Attached: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (summary of controls and options).

Best,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@novacare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novacare.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Recap: NovaCare discovery — data handling & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming on behalf of NovaCare:

- Training opt-out: confirmed. NovaCare data must not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood models. This applies to both prompt/response pairs and any derived embeddings.
- Retention: logs retained no longer than 30 days unless explicitly approved by NovaCare Security in writing.
- PII: we require that any PII be redacted or deterministically hashed before being persisted in logs. Hashing approach should be documented (salt management, rotation cadence).
- Residency: all processing and storage for NovaCare tenant must occur in the EU (eu-central-1). No cross-region backups without prior approval.

Security has asked that we include a short addendum to the MSA that references these specific constraints. Please send the addendum via DocuSign and include any SOC 2 evidence links you can share.

Attached: nova_security_requirements.pdf (security team note).

Anna Lewis
Head of Data Platforms
NovaCare Health
anna.lewis@novacare.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: DRAFT addendum language for NovaCare (internal)

Jordan / Marissa — draft language below for the training-opt-out addendum. This is intentionally short so it can be appended to the MSA as Exhibit A. Please review and let me know if you want any of the legal-y bits tightened before we send to NovaCare.

--- DRAFT EXHIBIT A — DATA HANDLING ADDENDUM (NOVACARE HEALTH) ---
1) Training prohibition: Except as explicitly authorized in writing by Customer (NovaCare Health), Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models or model weights, nor shall Redwood incorporate Customer Data into model evaluation datasets.
2) Logging & retention: Redwood shall retain inference logs associated with Customer Data for a maximum period of thirty (30) days, unless Customer provides prior written approval for a longer retention period.
3) PII handling: Redwood shall not persist raw personally identifiable information (PII) in logs. Where persistence of identifiers is necessary for operational debugging, Redwood shall persist only deterministically hashed identifiers using industry-standard hashing and salt management practices; salt rotation and access controls shall be documented.
4) Data residency: All processing, storage, and backups for Customer Data shall be restricted to the European Union (eu-central-1) unless Customer provides written consent for exceptions.

Attachments: training-optout-addendum-draft.docx

If everybody is good, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and include the SOC2 evidence link.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Counsel (Presales Legal)
Redwood Inference
